checks.name: 32/64/128/512-pad MSTs exactly match the original edges, ordering, net IDs and coordinates
Equal-distance grids, overlapping pads, rotations and shuffled footprint orders retain insertion-order ties
Deterministic random branching, disconnected, self-loop and duplicate-wire graphs match the legacy oracle
Subpixel, negative and large coordinates preserve Math.hypot comparison and deterministic output
Malformed nonfinite geometry uses deterministic compatibility fallback without hanging
Trace suppression preserves strict 0.05 tolerance, either direction, endpoint-only semantics and legacy net labels
Trace spatial buckets work across zero and negative boundaries with duplicate coincident routes
Unchanged and metadata-only nets reuse output without distance evaluations
One footprint movement rebuilds just its affected net and reuses other ratline objects
A footprint spanning several nets invalidates each changed pad net while reusing unrelated nets
Adding, editing, reordering and removing traces reuse MSTs and refresh only displayed suppression
Connectivity merge, split, reorder, missing endpoints and deleted pads invalidate safely
Cache keeps only current nets and footprints across repeated document replacement
Schematic synchronization retains per-net cache while preserving authored placement and trace arrays
An empty schematic releases its owned ratline caches before a same-ID replacement
